experiences.name: Angkor Wat Temple Complex Exploration
experiences.description: Spend a full day exploring the magnificent Angkor Wat temple complex, the largest religious monument in the world. Witness the stunning sunrise over the main temple, explore the intricate bas-reliefs depicting Hindu mythology, and discover the iconic Bayon temple with its 216 serene stone faces. Hire a local tuk-tuk driver for a guided small circuit tour covering Angkor Thom, Ta Prohm, and Angkor Wat itself.

experiences.name: Koh Rong Samloem Beach Retreat
experiences.description: Take a ferry to the pristine island of Koh Rong Samloem and spend the day on Saracen Bay or Lazy Beach, two of Cambodia's most breathtaking and unspoiled beaches. Enjoy crystal-clear turquoise waters, white sand, and excellent snorkeling among vibrant coral reefs. At night, witness the magical bioluminescent plankton glowing in the water — a truly unforgettable natural phenomenon.

experiences.name: Phnom Penh Historical Tour: Royal Palace & Killing Fields
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in Cambodia's complex history with a full-day tour of Phnom Penh's most significant sites. Visit the stunning Silver Pagoda and Royal Palace complex adorned with Khmer architecture, then pay solemn respects at the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison) and the Choeung Ek Killing Fields Memorial. This deeply moving experience provides essential context for understanding modern Cambodian culture and resilience.

experiences.name: Khmer Cooking Class & Phsar Thmei Market Tour
experiences.description: Begin with a guided tour of the iconic Art Deco Central Market (Phsar Thmei) to source fresh local ingredients including lemongrass, galangal, and kaffir lime leaves. Then join a hands-on Khmer cooking class where you'll learn to prepare traditional dishes such as Fish Amok (Cambodia's national dish), Lok Lak beef, and mango salad. Take home a recipe booklet and a deep appreciation for Cambodian culinary heritage.

experiences.name: Kampot River Kayaking & Pepper Plantation Tour
experiences.description: Paddle along the serene Kampot River through lush mangroves and past French colonial architecture in one of Cambodia's most charming riverside towns. Follow the kayaking with a guided tour of a traditional Kampot pepper plantation — home to some of the world's most prized peppercorns — and learn about the cultivation process. End the afternoon with a sunset cruise on the river and fresh seafood at a riverside restaurant.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Cambodia
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 13:00. Rest and transit time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Siem Reap International Airport at 13:00. Clear immigration, collect baggage, and arrange a tuk-tuk to your boutique stay near Angkor Archaeological Park (approx. $5–8 USD). Check in, freshen up, and take a slow walk around the immediate guesthouse area to get your bearings. Pop into a local convenience store or market stall to pick up water and snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Pub Street and the Old Market (Psar Chas) area in central Siem Reap — about 15–20 minutes by tuk-tuk. Stroll the lively night market, browse local crafts, and soak in the atmosphere. This is a great low-cost introduction to Cambodian street culture.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — in-flight meal or airport snack before landing.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite near the airport or at a roadside stall en route to the hotel — try a bowl of kuy teav (rice noodle soup) for under $2 USD.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Khmer Kitchen Restaurant near Pub Street — a beloved budget-friendly local spot. Try amok fish curry with jasmine rice for around $4–6 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Exchange some USD to Khmer Riel at the airport or a local money changer for small purchases. USD is widely accepted in Cambodia. Negotiate tuk-tuk fares before boarding. Keep Day 1 light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early (5:00–5:30 AM) for the iconic Angkor Wat sunrise — one of the most spectacular sights in Southeast Asia. Watch the temple's spires reflect in the lotus pond as dawn breaks. Purchase a 3-day Angkor Pass ($62 USD) at the ticket office — it's the best value if you plan to explore over multiple days. Spend the morning exploring Angkor Wat's bas-reliefs, galleries, and central towers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or cycle (rent a bicycle for $2–3/day near your guesthouse) to Angkor Thom, the ancient walled city. Visit the Bayon Temple with its 216 enigmatic stone faces, the Baphuon, and the Elephant Terrace. These are all within the same complex and included in your Angkor Pass.
day_by_day.evening: Return to your guesthouse to rest and clean up. Head into Siem Reap town for dinner and evening exploration of the Night Market on Sivatha Street.

meals.breakfast: Grab a baguette with egg and pâté from a street vendor near Angkor Wat for $1–2 USD — a French-Cambodian colonial classic.
meals.lunch: Pack snacks from the guesthouse or buy fruit and coconut water from vendors inside the Angkor complex (budget $2–3 USD).
meals.dinner: Try Marum Restaurant (training restaurant supporting street youth) — mains from $5–8 USD with excellent Khmer cuisine and a meaningful social impact.

day_by_day.notes: November weather in Cambodia is ideal — dry season just beginning, temperatures around 28–32°C. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and at least 1.5 liters of water. Wear modest clothing (covered shoulders and knees) as Angkor Wat is an active religious site. Sunrise entry is included in your pass.

day_by_day.morning: Use your Angkor Pass to visit Ta Prohm — the atmospheric jungle temple famously left partially unrestored, with massive tree roots engulfing the stone walls. It's quieter in the early morning. Then visit Banteay Kdei, a peaceful Buddhist monastery temple nearby.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cycle or tuk-tuk to Srah Srang, a royal bathing pool with a beautiful lakeside terrace — great for photos and reflection. Afterward, visit the smaller but exquisite Banteay Srei temple (about 25 km north of Siem Reap — best by tuk-tuk, ~$12–15 round trip). Known as the 'Citadel of Women,' it features incredibly detailed pink sandstone carvings.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Angkor National Museum near your accommodation area ($12 USD entry) for an in-depth understanding of Khmer history and the Angkor Empire. Alternatively, skip the museum fee and explore the free-to-browse artisan village of Artisans Angkor workshop nearby.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your guesthouse if included, or visit a local café for rice porridge (bobor) with egg — $1.50–2 USD.
meals.lunch: Roadside noodle stall near Banteay Srei village — fresh noodle soup or fried rice for $2–3 USD.
meals.dinner: Cook Street Food Tour or dine at Psar Leu (Central Market) food stalls — try lok lak (stir-fried beef with rice and egg) for $3–4 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Banteay Srei requires a short drive — negotiate a tuk-tuk day rate of $15–20 USD to cover all afternoon stops. Carry your Angkor Pass at all times. Stay hydrated and rest in shade during the hottest part of the day (12–2 PM).

day_by_day.morning: Use your final day on the Angkor Pass to explore the lesser-visited temples: Preah Khan (a sprawling monastic complex with long corridors and tree roots), Neak Pean (an island temple on an artificial lake — visually stunning), and Ta Som (small but beautifully preserved with a famous tree-covered eastern gopura).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Landmine Museum (free/donation-based, ~$5 suggested) located about 25 km from Siem Reap — a sobering and important educational experience about Cambodia's tragic history with landmines and the ongoing clearance efforts. Then head to the Cambodia Cultural Village ($7 entry) for a lighter look at traditional Khmer architecture, costumes, and miniature village replicas.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a traditional Apsara dance performance — check for free or low-cost shows at temples or budget venues. Koulen Restaurant offers a free Apsara show with dinner (meals from $6–10 USD).

meals.breakfast: French baguette sandwich from a roadside vendor near the guesthouse — $1.50 USD.
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch near Neak Pean — buy fresh fruit, rice cakes, and coconut water from vendors ($3 USD total).
meals.dinner: Koulen Restaurant for dinner with free Apsara dance performance — budget $8–10 USD for a full Khmer set meal.

day_by_day.notes: This is your last day using the Angkor 3-day pass — make the most of it. The Landmine Museum visit is highly recommended for historical context. Apsara performances are a UNESCO-recognized art form and a highlight of Cambodian culture.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning trip to the floating villages of Tonlé Sap Lake — Southeast Asia's largest freshwater lake. Book a budget boat tour ($10–15 USD) from the Chong Kneas or Kampong Phluk village dock. Witness entire communities living on stilted houses or floating platforms, with schools, churches, and markets on water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Siem Reap and visit the Preah Ang Chek Preah Ang Chorm Shrine near the Old Market — a free, locally revered shrine. Spend the afternoon exploring Siem Reap's colonial French Quarter on foot, admiring the architecture and stopping at local coffee shops.
day_by_day.evening: Check out the Siem Reap Art Center Night Market for handmade crafts, silk scarves, and artwork. Great for budget souvenir shopping. Enjoy a traditional Khmer massage at one of the many affordable spas ($7–10 for 1 hour).

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a local Khmer café — try nom banh chok (Khmer noodles with green fish curry sauce), a traditional breakfast dish, for $1.50–2 USD.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a riverside restaurant near Tonlé Sap — fresh fish amok or grilled fish with sticky rice for $4–5 USD.
meals.dinner: Street food dinner at the Old Market area — grilled skewers, spring rolls, and fresh fruit shakes for $3–5 USD total.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Tonlé Sap boat tour the evening before through your guesthouse to get the best rate. Avoid tours that feel exploitative of the communities — choose ethical operators. Kampong Phluk is more authentic and less touristy than Chong Kneas. Bring cash as card machines are rare on the lake.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take an early morning bus from Siem Reap to Phnom Penh (Cambodia's capital). Giant Ibis or Mekong Express buses are comfortable and reliable — tickets cost $10–13 USD for a 5–6 hour journey. Book in advance online. Depart by 7:00–8:00 AM.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Phnom Penh early afternoon. Check into a budget guesthouse near the riverside (dorms from $5–8/night, private rooms from $15–20/night). Drop your bags and head to the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda ($10 entry) — stunning royal architecture with gilded spires, sacred Buddha statues, and manicured gardens along the Mekong River.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the Sisowath Quay (riverside promenade) as the sun sets over the Tonlé Sap and Mekong rivers. Browse the evening food stalls and enjoy the lively local atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at the Siem Reap bus station café — baguette and coffee for $2 USD before boarding.
meals.lunch: Packed snacks on the bus or stop at a roadside rest stop en route — rice and curry for $2–3 USD.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Friends Restaurant (Mith Samlanh) near the riverside — a social enterprise training at-risk youth. Budget $6–9 USD for tapas-style Khmer dishes.

day_by_day.notes: Phnom Penh guesthouses fill up on weekends — book ahead. Store large luggage at your guesthouse while sightseeing. The Royal Palace closes at noon for lunch (12:00–2:00 PM) so time your visit accordingly. Tuk-tuks in Phnom Penh cost slightly more than Siem Reap — agree on price before riding.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison) — a former high school turned Khmer Rouge torture prison ($5 entry). This is one of the most important and sobering historical sites in all of Southeast Asia. Allow 2–3 hours for a thorough visit with the audio guide ($3 extra).
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a tuk-tuk to the Choeung Ek Genocidal Center (The Killing Fields), about 15 km from the city center ($3–4 tuk-tuk ride each way). Entry is $6 USD including an excellent audio guide. Pay respects at the memorial stupa and walk the peaceful grounds — a profoundly moving experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the city and visit the Phnom Penh Night Market (Phsar Reatrey) near the riverside — great for street food, local snacks, and affordable souvenirs. Decompress from the heavy historical sites with a riverside walk and a fresh coconut.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a local Khmer café near your guesthouse — fried rice with egg and iced coffee for $2–3 USD.
meals.lunch: Light lunch near Tuol Sleng — banh mi sandwich or fresh spring rolls from a street stall for $2 USD.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Romdeng Restaurant (sister to Friends Restaurant) — traditional Khmer cuisine in a colonial villa setting. Mains $6–9 USD. Try the tarantula appetizer if you're feeling adventurous!

day_by_day.notes: The Tuol Sleng and Killing Fields visits are emotionally intense — take your time and be respectful. Photography is permitted but be mindful. These sites are essential for understanding Cambodia's modern history. If you need emotional grounding afterward, the riverside park is a calm place to sit and reflect.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Central Market (Psar Thmei) — Phnom Penh's iconic Art Deco market with a massive yellow dome. Browse stalls selling jewelry, silk, electronics, and fresh produce. Great for budget shopping and people-watching. Then visit the nearby National Museum of Cambodia ($10 entry) — home to the world's finest collection of Khmer art and sculpture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel day: Take an afternoon bus or shared taxi from Phnom Penh to Sihanoukville (the gateway to Cambodia's beaches). Bus tickets cost $7–10 USD for a 4–5 hour journey. Alternatively, book a direct bus to Kampot ($6–8 USD, 3–4 hours) for a more charming, less developed coastal base. Arrive and check into a beach guesthouse.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Sihanoukville or Kampot and settle in. If in Kampot, take a slow evening walk along the Kampot River promenade — a laid-back, charming town with French colonial buildings and a relaxed vibe.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a riverside café in Phnom Penh — French toast with tropical fruit and iced coffee for $3 USD.
meals.lunch: Quick lunch near the Central Market before departure — noodle soup or fried rice for $2–3 USD.
meals.dinner: Dinner in Kampot at Rikitikitavi or a riverside restaurant — try Kampot pepper crab or fresh fish with local Kampot pepper (a world-famous specialty) for $6–9 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Kampot is strongly recommended over Sihanoukville for budget travelers seeking charm and culture — Sihanoukville has become heavily commercialized. Kampot is peaceful, affordable, and a great base for beach day trips. Book guesthouses in advance during November as the dry season brings more tourists.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Kep — a sleepy seaside town 25 km from Kampot. Hire a tuk-tuk for the day ($10–15 USD). Visit the famous Kep Crab Market and watch fishermen bring in the morning catch. Walk through Kep National Park along the jungle trail for panoramic sea views and monkey sightings (free entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Swim and relax at Kep Beach or take a short boat trip to Rabbit Island (Koh Tonsay) — one of Cambodia's most pristine and undeveloped islands ($5 USD return boat fare). Enjoy crystal-clear water, white sand, and hammocks strung between palm trees. No electricity or Wi-Fi — pure relaxation.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kampot by late afternoon. Enjoy a sunset kayak or boat cruise along the Kampot River through the mangroves ($8–12 USD per person). Watch fireflies emerge along the riverbanks as darkness falls — a magical experience.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Kampot guesthouse or a local café — banana pancakes and iced coffee for $2–3 USD.
meals.lunch: Fresh Kep crab cooked in Kampot pepper at the Kep Crab Market — a must-eat experience. Budget $8–12 USD for a whole crab with rice.
meals.dinner: Dinner back in Kampot at a riverside restaurant — fish amok or grilled prawns with rice for $5–7 USD. Watch the lights reflect on the river.

day_by_day.notes: Rabbit Island has basic bungalow accommodation if you want to spend the night ($10–15 USD) — a wonderful off-grid experience. Bring cash as there are no ATMs on the island. Sunscreen and insect repellent are essential. The Kampot firefly boat tour is best booked through your guesthouse the evening before.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Kampot — visit the Bokor Hill Station by motorbike taxi or organized tour ($10–15 USD). The hill station sits 1,080 meters above sea level inside Preah Monivong National Park. Explore the eerie abandoned French colonial casino, the old Catholic church, and enjoy sweeping views over the Gulf of Thailand and the Cambodian coastline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Kampot for a final leisurely lunch. Browse the small artisan shops along the riverside for last-minute souvenirs — look for locally made Kampot pepper products, silk items, and handcrafted jewelry. Pack your bags and arrange transport back to Phnom Penh airport or your next destination (bus $6–8 USD, 3–4 hours).
day_by_day.evening: If flying out of Phnom Penh, arrive at the airport with ample time. Spend any remaining Khmer Riel on snacks or small gifts at the airport. Reflect on an incredible 10 days of Cambodian history, culture, and natural beauty.

meals.breakfast: Final Cambodian breakfast — nom banh chok (Khmer noodles) at a local market stall for $1.50 USD.
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch at a Kampot riverside restaurant — Khmer red curry with fresh baguette and a cold Angkor beer for $5–7 USD.
meals.dinner: Airport meal or snacks if departing — or a final Phnom Penh dinner at a local restaurant near the bus station for $4–6 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 4–5 hours travel time from Kampot to Phnom Penh International Airport. Book your return bus in advance. Spend any remaining Riel before leaving — it cannot be exchanged outside Cambodia. Tip your tuk-tuk drivers and guesthouse staff generously — service workers earn very little. Cambodia is an unforgettable destination — consider leaving a positive review for ethical local businesses you encountered.

trip_options.title: Classic Cambodia Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00. Rest and freshen up after landing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to your boutique stay near Angkor Archaeological Park. Take a gentle orientation stroll around the hotel grounds and nearby Siem Reap Old Market (Phsar Chas) area to get your bearings, pick up a local SIM card, and exchange currency.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Pub Street and the surrounding night market on foot. Browse local handicrafts and silk scarves at the Angkor Night Market. Enjoy a relaxed first evening soaking in the atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at Siem Reap International Airport or a café near the hotel upon arrival — try a bowl of Khmer noodle soup (kuy teav) at a local spot for ~$3–5.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Mahob Restaurant near Old Market — a well-regarded mid-range Khmer restaurant serving amok fish curry and lok lak beef. Budget ~$10–15 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Do not over-schedule Day 1. Jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Purchase a 3-day or 7-day Angkor Pass at the official ticket office (open until 17:30) if you plan to visit the temples starting Day 2 — it saves time in the morning queue.

day_by_day.morning: Early rise for sunrise at Angkor Wat (arrive by 05:30). Watch the iconic reflection of the temple towers in the lotus pond as the sun rises — one of Southeast Asia's most memorable sights. Explore the outer galleries and bas-reliefs depicting the Churning of the Ocean of Milk.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Angkor Thom complex: visit the Bayon Temple (famous for its 216 giant stone faces), the Baphuon, Phimeanakas, and the Terrace of the Elephants. Take a tuk-tuk between sites (~$15–20 for a full-day driver).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siem Reap town. Attend a traditional Apsara dance performance at Koulen II Restaurant or Smile of Angkor — a cultural highlight showcasing ancient Khmer court dance. Dinner included at the venue.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at your hotel or grab a baguette and coffee from a street stall near the temple entrance (~$2–3).
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local restaurant near Angkor Thom — try Blue Pumpkin Angkor or a roadside Khmer eatery for rice dishes and fresh spring rolls (~$6–8).
meals.dinner: Dinner with Apsara show at Koulen II (~$18–25 per person including buffet) or return to Old Market area for à la carte dining at Haven Restaurant, a social enterprise training Cambodian youth (~$10–14).

day_by_day.notes: November weather in Siem Reap is ideal — dry season begins, temperatures around 28–32°C. Wear light, breathable clothing and bring sunscreen and a hat. Stay hydrated. Angkor Pass is required — buy it the evening before (Day 1) to maximize morning time.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Ta Prohm — the jungle temple famously left partially unrestored, with massive strangler fig and silk-cotton trees growing through the ruins (made famous by Tomb Raider). Arrive early (~07:00) before tour groups arrive for a more atmospheric experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Banteay Srei, located about 25 km northeast of Siem Reap. Known as the 'Citadel of Women,' this 10th-century temple is celebrated for its intricate pink sandstone carvings — considered the finest in all of Angkor. En route, stop at the Landmine Museum to learn about Cambodia's history with UXO and ongoing demining efforts.
day_by_day.evening: Back in Siem Reap, visit the Angkor National Museum for a deeper understanding of Khmer civilization, artifacts, and the history of the Angkor Empire. Open until 18:30. (~$12 entry fee)

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local bakery — try a Cambodian rice porridge (babor) with ginger and pork at a street stall (~$2).
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch near Banteay Srei or eat at a local family-run restaurant in the village nearby (~$5–7).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Cuisine Wat Damnak — one of Siem Reap's most acclaimed restaurants offering a modern Khmer tasting menu using local seasonal ingredients. Book ahead. (~$30–35 per person, set menu).

day_by_day.notes: Hire a tuk-tuk for the full day to cover the distance to Banteay Srei comfortably (~$20–25). The Landmine Museum is a sobering but important cultural stop — donations appreciated. Banteay Srei is not covered by the standard Angkor Pass — check current ticketing rules.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Preah Khan — a large flat temple complex built by Jayavarman VII, less crowded than Angkor Wat but equally impressive, with long corridors, carved doorways, and atmospheric tree roots. Then walk to nearby Neak Pean, a small island temple set in an artificial pond symbolizing the Himalayan lake Anavatapta.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a boat trip on Tonlé Sap Lake — the largest freshwater lake in Southeast Asia. Visit a floating village (Kampong Phluk is more authentic and less touristy than Chong Kneas). See stilted houses, floating schools, and local life on the water. (~$15–20 for boat tour)
day_by_day.evening: Free evening in Siem Reap. Explore Kandal Village — a quieter, more boutique neighborhood with independent cafés, art galleries, and design shops. Great for a relaxed walk and souvenir shopping.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a riverside restaurant near the Tonlé Sap departure point — fresh fish dishes are a specialty (~$7–10).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Malis Restaurant — upscale Cambodian cuisine in a beautiful garden setting. Try the signature Khmer sampler platter. (~$15–20 per person).

day_by_day.notes: November is a great time to visit Tonlé Sap — the lake is at or near its maximum size after the monsoon season, making floating village access easier. Bring insect repellent for the lake excursion. Wear shoes you don't mind getting wet.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Siem Reap by morning bus or private transfer to Phnom Penh (~6 hours by bus, ~$12–15 via Giant Ibis or Mekong Express, or ~$80–100 by private car). Enjoy the countryside scenery along the way.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Phnom Penh early-to-mid afternoon. Check in to your guesthouse or mid-range hotel near the Riverside (Sisowath Quay area recommended). Take a walk along the Mekong Riverside promenade to stretch your legs and get oriented.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda (check closing times — usually 17:00, may need to visit early next morning). If closed, stroll the palace exterior and Riverside at golden hour, then explore the Night Market along Sisowath Quay.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at hotel before departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch on the bus or at a rest stop en route — packed snacks or a quick Cambodian meal at a roadside stop (~$4–6).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Romdeng Restaurant in Phnom Penh — a social enterprise serving traditional Cambodian cuisine in a colonial villa. Famous for its fried tarantulas (adventurous option) and amok. (~$12–18 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Book your bus ticket from Siem Reap to Phnom Penh in advance, especially for premium operators like Giant Ibis which offer comfortable seats, WiFi, and reliability. Alternatively, a 45-minute domestic flight is available for ~$50–80 if you prefer speed. Accommodation in Phnom Penh not specified — book a mid-range hotel near Riverside for convenience.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda (open from 08:00). Admire the Throne Hall, the Moonlight Pavilion, and the Silver Pagoda housing the Emerald Buddha and a life-size gold Buddha encrusted with 9,584 diamonds. Dress modestly — shoulders and knees covered. (~$10 entry)
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the National Museum of Cambodia — a stunning terracotta building housing the world's finest collection of Khmer art, including statues from Angkor spanning centuries. (~$10 entry). Afterward, walk to the Central Market (Phsar Thmei) — a stunning Art Deco dome market for browsing jewelry, clothing, and souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cruise on the Mekong and Tonlé Sap confluence — a beautiful way to see Phnom Penh from the water as the city lights up. Many operators offer 1–1.5 hour cruises (~$10–15). Return for dinner in the Riverside area.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a riverside café — try a French-Cambodian baguette sandwich (nom pang) with pâté and pickled vegetables, a colonial-era legacy (~$2–3).
meals.lunch: Lunch at Friends the Restaurant (Phsar Chas area) — another social enterprise training at-risk youth, offering tapas-style Cambodian dishes. (~$8–12).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Khmer Surin — authentic Khmer cuisine with a lovely garden ambiance near the Riverside. (~$10–15 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Phnom Penh is more urban and traffic-heavy than Siem Reap. Use PassApp tuk-tuks (app-based, like Uber for tuk-tuks) for safe and fairly priced transport around the city. Dress codes apply at the Royal Palace.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21) — the former high school turned Khmer Rouge prison where an estimated 17,000 people were tortured and executed. A deeply sobering but essential historical experience for understanding Cambodia's recent past. Allow 2–3 hours. (~$8 entry, audio guide recommended)
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a half-day trip to the Killing Fields of Choeung Ek (~15 km from city center, ~$5 tuk-tuk ride). The memorial stupa and audio guide (included in $6 entry) provide a powerful and moving account of the genocide. Return to the city by mid-afternoon for some quiet reflection time.
day_by_day.evening: Lighter evening — browse the Russian Market (Phsar Tuol Tom Poung) for handicrafts, silk, and local goods before it closes (~17:00–18:00). Then enjoy a peaceful dinner and early night.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local coffee shop — Cambodian iced coffee (café touk doh ko) with condensed milk is a must-try.
meals.lunch: Light lunch after the Killing Fields — eat at a simple local restaurant near Choeung Ek or back in the city. Khmer rice with vegetables (~$4–6). Given the emotional weight of the morning, keep lunch simple.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Sugar Palm Phnom Penh — elegant Cambodian restaurant with refined versions of traditional dishes. (~$12–18 per person).

day_by_day.notes: The Tuol Sleng and Killing Fields visits are emotionally heavy. Give yourself time and space to process. Many travelers find it helpful to visit these sites together on one day and allow the evening to be calm and reflective. Not recommended for young children. Hire a guide for deeper historical context (~$10–15).

day_by_day.morning: Depart Phnom Penh for Sihanoukville by bus (~4–5 hours, ~$10–12 via Giant Ibis or Cambodian Bus) or take a direct bus/van to Kep or Kampot (~3 hours, ~$8–10) — a more charming coastal alternative. Kampot is strongly recommended for a mid-range traveler seeking authentic beach and culture experiences.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Kampot. Check in to a mid-range guesthouse or boutique hotel along the Kampot River (many charming options for $30–60/night). Explore the charming French colonial Old Town on foot — colorful shop-houses, riverside promenade, and the iconic Durian Roundabout.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset kayaking or boat cruise on the Kampot River through mangroves — a magical experience as fireflies begin to glow at dusk. Many guesthouses and tour operators offer this for ~$10–15.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch on the bus or at a stop en route — or arrive and eat at a riverside café in Kampot (~$5–8).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Rikitikitavi — a beloved Kampot institution with a mix of Khmer and international dishes and a beautiful riverside terrace. (~$8–14 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Kampot is far preferable to Sihanoukville for mid-range travelers seeking culture and beaches — Sihanoukville has undergone significant overdevelopment. Kampot offers a relaxed, authentic atmosphere with excellent food, nearby beaches, and the famous Bokor National Park. Book accommodation in advance as good spots fill up.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Kep — a small, laid-back seaside town 25 km from Kampot, famous for its crab market and the nearby Kep National Park. Rent a bicycle or take a tuk-tuk (~$10 return). Visit the Crab Market and browse the stalls of freshly caught seafood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike the trails of Kep National Park through jungle to viewpoints overlooking the Gulf of Thailand and Rabbit Island (Koh Tonsay). Alternatively, take a short boat to Rabbit Island itself (~$5 return) for a few hours on a beautiful, quiet beach with clear water and minimal development.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kampot. Visit Kampot's famous pepper plantations — Kampot pepper is world-renowned and a UNESCO-recognized product. Many farms offer late afternoon tours (~$5–8). End the evening with a relaxed riverside walk.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Kampot guesthouse or a riverside café — try a Khmer breakfast of rice porridge or a fresh baguette.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Kep Crab Market — eat freshly grilled or stir-fried crab with Kampot pepper sauce directly from the market stalls. One of Cambodia's great culinary experiences. (~$8–12).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Baraka in Kampot — a charming garden restaurant with excellent Khmer and Mediterranean fusion dishes. (~$8–13 per person).

day_by_day.notes: November weather on the coast is excellent — dry and sunny with calm seas. Perfect for beach and island visits. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a hat, and water. The Kep crab lunch is a highlight not to be missed — arrive at the market between 11:00–13:00 for the freshest selection.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Kampot — take a slow morning. Visit Phnom Chhngok Cave Temple (~8 km from Kampot) — a limestone cave hiding a small ancient Khmer temple inside, with beautiful stalactites and local spiritual significance. (~$1 entry, hire a local guide for $3–5).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Kampot town. Last-minute souvenir shopping — buy authentic Kampot pepper, locally made crafts, and silk items. Head to the bus station for an afternoon bus back to Phnom Penh (~3 hours) if flying out, or to Siem Reap if needed for a return flight.
day_by_day.evening: Depending on your departure logistics — if flying from Phnom Penh, arrive in the city by early evening, have a final Cambodian dinner near the airport or Riverside, and prepare for departure. If your flight is the following day, enjoy a final relaxed evening.

meals.breakfast: Final Cambodian breakfast — a full spread at your guesthouse or a local market breakfast of rice, eggs, and fresh fruit (~$3–5).
meals.lunch: Light lunch in Kampot before departure — try a fresh coconut shake and a Khmer sandwich at a riverside café (~$4–6).
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner — if in Phnom Penh, return to a favorite restaurant or try Topaz Restaurant for a special upscale Cambodian-French farewell meal (~$20–30 per person). If still in transit, a simple but satisfying local meal (~$8–12).

day_by_day.notes: Allow plenty of travel time on the final day. Phnom Penh International Airport is the main hub — arrive at least 2.5–3 hours before international departure. Confirm your return bus or transfer booking the night before. Consider buying extra Kampot pepper as gifts — it's lightweight, affordable, and a uniquely Cambodian souvenir. Safe travels!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Cambodia Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Siem Reap International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer awaits at the airport with a welcome refreshment and cool towel service.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check-in at your boutique luxury stay within the Angkor Archaeological Park area. Settle in, enjoy a welcome drink and property orientation. Take a leisurely stroll around the hotel grounds and pool to decompress from travel. Optional: light spa treatment (aromatherapy or jet-lag relief massage) at the hotel spa.
day_by_day.evening: Gentle introduction to Siem Reap with a private tuk-tuk ride through the Old Market (Phsar Chas) district. Browse artisan shops and silk boutiques at a relaxed pace before heading to dinner.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight or airport lounge
meals.lunch: Welcome lunch at the hotel restaurant featuring Khmer set menu with fresh coconut water and local seasonal fruits
meals.dinner: Dinner at Cuisine Wat Damnak — one of Cambodia's most acclaimed fine-dining restaurants offering a seasonal Khmer tasting menu with wine pairings (advance reservation essential)

day_by_day.notes: Ensure your hotel has arranged airport pickup in advance. November is the start of Cambodia's dry and cool season — expect pleasant temperatures around 25–28°C. Light linen clothing recommended. Keep hydrated after the flight.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn private sunrise tour of Angkor Wat (depart hotel at 05:00). Watch the iconic temple silhouette reflect in the lotus ponds as the sun rises — a truly magical experience. Your private guide will provide historical context on the 12th-century Khmer masterpiece. Explore the outer galleries, bas-reliefs depicting the Churning of the Ocean of Milk, and the inner sanctum.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Angkor Thom, the last great capital of the Khmer Empire. Visit the Bayon Temple with its 216 serene stone faces, the Baphuon, Phimeanakas, and the Terrace of the Elephants. Return to the hotel for a midday rest and lunch during the hottest hours.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a rooftop bar overlooking rice fields or the Angkor skyline. Attend an exclusive Apsara Dance performance — a classical Khmer ballet listed as UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage — at a premium venue such as Amansara or a temple courtyard setting.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast box prepared by the hotel (fruit, pastries, coffee) taken at Angkor Wat at sunrise
meals.lunch: Return to hotel for a full Khmer brunch/lunch — try amok trey (fish amok in coconut curry) and lok lak (Cambodian beef stir-fry)
meals.dinner: Dinner at the Apsara performance venue or at Mahob Restaurant at Park Hyatt Siem Reap — refined Cambodian cuisine in an elegant colonial setting

day_by_day.notes: Bring a light layer for the early morning as temperatures can dip to 20°C before sunrise. Dress modestly for temple visits (shoulders and knees covered). A private licensed English-speaking guide is highly recommended and can be arranged through the hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Ta Prohm — the jungle temple famously left partially unrestored, with massive silk-cotton and strangler fig trees enveloping the stone walls. Best explored early before crowds arrive. Your guide will narrate its history as a Buddhist monastery and its Hollywood fame. Continue to Banteay Kdei, a quieter temple with beautiful devata carvings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided visit to Banteay Srei — the 'Citadel of Women,' located 25 km north of Angkor. This 10th-century temple is renowned for its extraordinarily intricate pink sandstone carvings, considered the finest examples of Khmer decorative art. En route, stop at the Landmine Museum to learn about Cambodia's modern history and ongoing demining efforts.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siem Reap for an exclusive private cooking class with a master Khmer chef. Learn to prepare traditional dishes including fish amok, green mango salad, and sticky rice desserts in a luxury villa kitchen setting.

meals.breakfast: Full à la carte breakfast at the hotel — eggs Benedict, fresh tropical fruit platters, Cambodian rice porridge (bobor)
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch arranged by the hotel and enjoyed in the shade near Banteay Srei — gourmet sandwiches, cold-pressed juices, and local snacks
meals.dinner: Enjoy the dishes you prepared during the cooking class, served formally with Cambodian wine or craft cocktails

day_by_day.notes: Banteay Srei requires a 45-minute drive each way — arrange a comfortable air-conditioned vehicle. The cooking class can be booked through the hotel concierge; top providers include Nary Kitchen or a private villa experience. Carry sunscreen and a hat for afternoon outdoor visits.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the lesser-visited but spectacular Preah Khan temple — a vast monastic complex with long corridors, hidden courtyards, and atmospheric moss-covered stones. Then visit Neak Pean, an artificial island temple built on a circular island in a reservoir, accessible by a wooden walkway. Finish with Ta Som, a small but beautifully preserved late 12th-century temple.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Angkor National Museum in Siem Reap for an air-conditioned deep dive into Khmer civilization — over 1,000 artifacts including Buddha statues, royal regalia, and multimedia exhibits on Angkor's history. Afterward, visit a premium silk weaving atelier such as Artisans Angkor to observe master craftspeople and purchase authentic Cambodian silk products.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset boat cruise on the Tonlé Sap Lake — the largest freshwater lake in Southeast Asia. Observe floating villages, local fishing life, and a spectacular sunset over the water from a private chartered boat with champagne service.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — Cambodian congee with ginger and pork, fresh baguette with local honey, tropical fruit juices
meals.lunch: Lunch at a riverside restaurant in Siem Reap — try Malis Restaurant for elevated Khmer cuisine with a garden setting
meals.dinner: Private dinner on the boat during the sunset cruise, or at Haven Restaurant — a social enterprise training young Cambodians in hospitality, offering excellent Western and Khmer fusion cuisine

day_by_day.notes: The Tonlé Sap boat cruise should be booked through a reputable operator via your hotel concierge. November is an excellent time as the lake is at near-maximum size following the rainy season. Bring a light jacket for the evening on the water.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Koh Ker — a remote ancient capital located 120 km northeast of Siem Reap (approximately 2-hour drive). This UNESCO-listed site features the dramatic seven-tiered pyramid temple Prasat Thom, rising 36 meters above the jungle canopy. Explore the sprawling complex with your private guide — far fewer tourists than Angkor, offering an authentic archaeological adventure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Beng Mealea — a 12th-century temple of similar scale to Angkor Wat but left almost entirely to the jungle. Walk along wooden boardwalks through collapsed galleries draped in roots and vines. This is one of Cambodia's most atmospheric and photogenic sites.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siem Reap (approximately 1.5 hours). Freshen up and enjoy a premium spa evening at the hotel — opt for a traditional Khmer herbal compress massage or a couples' treatment in a private villa suite.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure — continental spread with fresh pastries, cold cuts, and Cambodian coffee
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet picnic lunch prepared by the hotel, enjoyed at Koh Ker amid the ancient ruins
meals.dinner: Dinner at Embassy Restaurant or Spoons Restaurant in Siem Reap — both offer refined Cambodian and international menus in elegant surroundings

day_by_day.notes: This is a full-day excursion — depart by 07:00 to maximize time at both sites. An air-conditioned private vehicle is essential. Wear sturdy walking shoes as Beng Mealea involves climbing over some rubble. Carry 2–3 liters of water per person. The road to Koh Ker is paved and in good condition.

day_by_day.morning: Private helicopter transfer from Siem Reap to Phnom Penh (approximately 45 minutes) for a dramatic aerial view of the Cambodian landscape, Mekong River, and Tonlé Sap. Check in at a luxury Phnom Penh hotel (Raffles Hotel Le Royal or Rosewood Phnom Penh recommended). Visit the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda — the official residence of the King of Cambodia, featuring the stunning Throne Hall, Moonlight Pavilion, and the Silver Pagoda with its emerald Buddha.
day_by_day.afternoon: Sobering but essential visit to the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison) and the Choeung Ek Memorial (Killing Fields) — powerful sites that provide crucial context on Cambodia's tragic Khmer Rouge history (1975–1979). A private guide with sensitivity and expertise is essential here.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the Elephant Bar at Raffles Hotel Le Royal — a legendary colonial-era bar that has hosted royalty, journalists, and dignitaries. Then explore the Riverside Promenade along the Tonlé Sap River as locals gather for the evening.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at Siem Reap hotel before helicopter departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at Topaz Restaurant in Phnom Penh — a long-standing fine dining institution with French-Cambodian cuisine and an excellent wine cellar
meals.dinner: Dinner at Malis Phnom Penh — the flagship location of Cambodia's most celebrated Khmer fine dining restaurant, helmed by Chef Luu Meng

day_by_day.notes: The helicopter transfer can be arranged through Helistar Cambodia. Book well in advance. The Tuol Sleng and Choeung Ek visits are emotionally heavy — allocate 3–4 hours and consider the timing carefully. These sites close in the late afternoon. Dress respectfully at all historic and memorial sites.

day_by_day.morning: Morning visit to the National Museum of Cambodia — Southeast Asia's largest repository of Khmer art, housing over 14,000 artifacts including the world's finest collection of Khmer sculpture. Explore the beautiful terracotta pavilions and tranquil courtyard. Afterward, browse the Russian Market (Psar Toul Tom Poung) for premium silk scarves, silverware, and Khmer antiques.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private speedboat charter along the Mekong River to Koh Dach (Silk Island) — a peaceful island community 15 km from Phnom Penh where traditional silk weaving has been practiced for generations. Visit weaving families in their homes and observe the intricate hand-loom process. Return by boat to Phnom Penh.
day_by_day.evening: Private transfer to Phnom Penh International Airport for an evening flight south to Sihanoukville, then onward by private transfer to Koh Rong Samloem or Song Saa Private Island for the beach portion of the trip. Alternatively, take a luxury private vehicle transfer (approximately 3.5 hours).

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Phnom Penh — full buffet or à la carte at the hotel restaurant
meals.lunch: Lunch on Koh Dach island — fresh Mekong fish grilled over charcoal, green papaya salad, and coconut desserts prepared by a local family
meals.dinner: Dinner at Song Saa Private Island resort upon arrival, or at a premium beachfront restaurant in Koh Rong Samloem

day_by_day.notes: Song Saa Private Island is Cambodia's most exclusive luxury island resort and requires advance booking (often months ahead). Alternatively, Koh Rong Samloem's Lazy Beach or Saracen Bay area offers premium boutique options. Confirm transfer logistics with your hotel concierge before this day.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up to pristine turquoise waters and white sand beaches. Morning snorkeling or scuba diving excursion around the coral reefs of Koh Rong Samloem or the Song Saa Marine Reserve — one of Cambodia's most biodiverse marine areas. Spot reef fish, sea turtles, and vibrant coral gardens. Equipment and a certified guide provided by the resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Beach relaxation on a secluded private beach — enjoy a beachside massage, read, or kayak along the coastline. Optional: stand-up paddleboarding or sailing on a traditional Cambodian boat. Explore the island's interior jungle trail to a hidden waterfall (seasonal).
day_by_day.evening: Private beach bonfire dinner arranged by the resort — fresh seafood barbecue including Cambodian lobster, tiger prawns, and catch-of-the-day fish, served under the stars with chilled white wine and cocktails.

meals.breakfast: Tropical breakfast delivered to your villa or beachside — fresh papaya, mango, coconut pancakes, eggs to order, and cold-pressed juices
meals.lunch: Light beach club lunch — grilled fish tacos, fresh ceviche, tropical fruit smoothies, and coconut water
meals.dinner: Private beach bonfire seafood barbecue with sommelier-selected wines and cocktails

day_by_day.notes: November is ideal for the Cambodian coast — the Gulf of Thailand side (Koh Rong) typically has calm seas and clear skies. Bring reef-safe sunscreen. The resort can arrange all water sports and activities. Bioluminescent plankton may be visible in the water after dark — ask the resort for a night swim experience.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning fishing trip with local fishermen — depart at dawn on a traditional wooden boat, learn traditional Cambodian fishing techniques, and enjoy the serene beauty of the Gulf of Thailand at sunrise. Return with your catch for a special lunch preparation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Island hopping by private speedboat to nearby uninhabited islands — visit Koh Prins, Koh Tang, or other nearby islets for secluded swimming, snorkeling, and picnicking. Explore sea caves and hidden lagoons accessible only by boat.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a private sunset yoga session on the beach or a rooftop deck. Followed by a traditional Khmer herbal bath ritual and couples' spa treatment at the resort spa — using locally sourced ingredients like lemongrass, kaffir lime, and galangal.

meals.breakfast: Light pre-departure breakfast before fishing trip — fruit, yogurt, granola, and Cambodian coffee
meals.lunch: Your morning catch prepared by the resort chef in your preferred style — grilled, steamed with ginger, or in a traditional Khmer curry, served beachside
meals.dinner: Fine dining at the resort's main restaurant — multi-course tasting menu featuring Cambodian coastal cuisine with international influences and curated wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: The fishing trip should be arranged through the resort the day before. Island hopping routes depend on sea conditions and the captain's recommendation. Bring waterproof bags for electronics on the boat. Confirm spa appointments in advance as slots fill quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — wake early for a peaceful solo sunrise walk along the beach or a guided meditation session on the shore. Pack and check out at leisure. Private speedboat transfer back to the mainland (Sihanoukville or Koh Kong depending on departure route).
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time: optional stop in Sihanoukville for a final browse of local markets and a farewell Cambodian coffee. Alternatively, transfer directly to Phnom Penh International Airport or Siem Reap for your onward flight. En route, reflect on the journey with a curated photo book or journal of your 10-day experience (many luxury hotels offer this as a complimentary farewell gift).
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Cambodia. Airport lounge access recommended — Priority Pass or dedicated premium lounge available at Phnom Penh International Airport.

meals.breakfast: Farewell breakfast at the resort — full spread with your favorite dishes from the week, fresh tropical juices, and Cambodian specialty coffee (Kampot pepper coffee or Mondulkiri robusta)
meals.lunch: Light farewell lunch at the airport or a riverside restaurant in Sihanoukville — fresh spring rolls, grilled lemongrass chicken, and mango sticky rice as a final taste of Cambodia
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Ensure your return transfer is booked well in advance — speedboat schedules from the islands are fixed and must align with your flight time. Allow at least 4–5 hours from island departure to international flight check-in. Consider purchasing Kampot pepper, Cambodian coffee, and silk items as premium souvenirs. Tipping guides, drivers, and hotel staff is customary and appreciated — budget approximately $10–20 USD per day for guides and $5–10 for drivers.
